# [**GA4 Exam Certification**]{.underline}

![](image1.png)

## [**Exam Reflection**]{.underline}

### [**Results Summary**]{.underline}

*Pass — 94% score. The outcome indicates that there is solid knowledge of Google analytics 4 concepts, including events, dimensions and audiences and reporting tools. A score of more than 90 per cent proves that the core GA4 framework was used appropriately in the majority of the questions, such as data streams, acquisition reports, and BigQuery exports. The certification proves that the exam is successfully completed and is offered to the person who can properly analyze user behavior and the performance of the marketing application with the help of the GA4 tools and reports.*

### [**Top 3 Most challenging topics**]{.underline}

-   *Acquisition vs. Traffic Acquisitions report: The difference between first user source and session source was to be given serious consideration since both reports are used to measure acquisition at varying levels.*

-   *GA4 exploration methods: To distinguish the three analysis methods of free-form exploration, funnel exploration and segment overlap, further conceptual insights of when each analysis technique should be used would be needed.*

-   *Parameters of events, event dimension and event metrics: It could be difficult to differentiate between these concepts since they are all associated with the manner in which data is recorded and reported in GA4.*

### [**Two of the Questions I Wish I Could Redo**]{.underline}

*The difference between metrics and dimensions in reporting is one of the concepts I would re-examine. Although I know that measures are quantifiable, and characteristics are qualifiable by dimension, there were questions that demanded the application of their difference in a reporting setting. The other concept that I would repeat is connected with the customization and navigation of the report, e.g., being aware of the instances when I would use Library, Explore, or Admin to handle reports or adjust the reporting views in GA4.*

### [**CEP Connection (Google Demo Account)**]{.underline}

*An example of the change I will incorporate in my Customer Engagement Plan (CEP) measurement strategy is the establishment of a funnel exploration that would trace the route through visits to the homepage all the way to critical events like purchases or sign-ups in the Google Analytics experiencing account. In the Traffic Acquisition report, I am also going to identify key events (conversion) and group them by their source/medium of sessions. This will assist in determining the marketing channels with the most valuable user behavior and make better optimization decisions.*

#### [GA4 “readiness check” (required; CEP or Google demo)]{.underline}

![](image2.png)

***Engagement-Events-Referrals/Emails Comparison***

*Using the Google Analytics demo account, the KPI I selected is **Event Count**, which measures how many engagement interactions users perform on the website. The supporting report is the **Engagement → Events report**, where I compared engagement generated from **referral and email traffic sources**. This KPI supports my project goal because event counts show how actively users interact with the site after arriving from different marketing channels. By comparing referral and email traffic, I can determine which channel drives more meaningful engagement. This helps identify the most effective traffic sources for improving user interaction and marketing performance.*
